column1: # The rename mapping: the old Plus Suite vocabulary to daedalus's, one table for
# every consumer. The code-rename script beside the parent topic note
# this file by default) rewrites a source tree with it and gates a renamed
# tree on it; Drupal\daedalus\Migrate\PlusSuite\Mapping translates a site's persisted
# state with it (config, key_value, layout sections). Tab-separated:
# kind <TAB> old <TAB> new <TAB> note (tabs, because the regex kinds use `|`).
# Kinds decide the boundaries around the literal `old`:
#   id      machine names, entity types, paths, namespaces, human names:
#           not preceded or followed by [A-Za-z0-9]; `_` may follow, so a
#           machine name doubles as the prefix of its sub-modules, hooks,
#           plugin IDs, config, routes, services and permissions.
#   prefix  like id but nothing is checked after.
#   camel   UpperCamel prefix: not preceded by [A-Z], not followed by [a-z].
#   lcamel  lowerCamel prefix: not preceded by [A-Za-z0-9], not followed by [a-z].
#   regex   a raw perl/PCRE regex with $1/$2 in `new`, run before the literal pass.
#   protect a raw regex whose matches survive untouched (masked, then restored).
#   keep    a deliberate old-name site in the source tree: masked like protect;
#           the script reports them and never gates them.
#   forbid  a literal that must not occur in the source tree at all (script only).
#   floor   the oldest system.schema version of an old module the site
#           migration serves (`new` is the version; the audit refuses below it).
#   skip    a regex over repo-relative paths (directories carry a trailing `/`)
#           the script never scans, renames or gates; Mapping ignores these rows.
# Literal patterns are tried at every position id/prefix/lcamel first, then
# camel, longest first within each (ties in table order), and every pattern
# refuses a `daedalus`/`Daedalus` immediately before it, which makes the
# mapping idempotent. The script's header documents the rules in full.
# --- machine names (module, theme, recipe projects); sub-modules, hooks,
# --- plugin IDs, config, schema, routes, services, libraries, permissions
# --- and PHP namespaces follow by prefix.
